chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddaq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the woman who is struck by labor pains for days or two days and sees yellowness or blood, he said: 'She should pray as long as she does not give birth. So if the pain overcomes her and she misses a prayer, unable to perform it due to the pain, then upon her is the making up of that prayer after she becomes clean.'

key_terms.الصُّفْرَةَ: Yellowness (a type of post-childbirth or menstrual discharge)
key_terms.الطَّلْقُ: Labor pains or onset of childbirth
key_terms.الْوَجَعُ: Pain (specifically labor pain in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prayer for a woman in labor who sees blood before giving birth?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the status of a woman in prolonged labor (talq), ruling that she remains in the state of prayer (salat) rather than menstruation (hayd) until actual delivery, provided she can endure the pain. It introduces a practical nuance for severe labor: if pain prevents prayer, the missed prayers are deferred and made up (qada) after purification, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of removing hardship (raf' al-haraj). This distinction is crucial for distinguishing between pre-birth bleeding and true menstruation, ensuring continuous worship during the critical transition period.
